correctness.rationale: The original Cao–Pan Theorem 2 is used with exact hypotheses alpha>=2 and n>=1, extended to all x in Z_2 by continuity and mod-four sign periodicity. The Narayana series converges uniformly, agrees with S_n for every n>=1, but not S_0. Direct exact sums give S(0)=S(1)=2, S(-2)=S(-1)=-2, hence D(0)=D(-2)=0. Subtracting the two shifted Cao–Pan congruences yields a nonzero leading term 2^(alpha+2) mod 2^(alpha+3) for even indices; odd telescoping preserves the leading term. The two zero anchors classify every even index; alpha=1 covers odd indices. Congruence classes give full natural densities. Finite checker reproduces 2030 test indices and modular identities, supplemental only.

value.rationale: Determines a natural and previously unevaluated arithmetic invariant for all positive indices of a classical counting sequence, including absence of valuation three and exact density at every higher level. The nontrivial content is the identification of two two-adic zeros and isometric branches which explain, rather than merely tabulate, the entire prime-power divisibility pattern. No generalization to other primes is claimed.
